title: FLDetector: Defending Federated Learning Against Model Poisoning Attacks via Detecting Malicious Clients

problem.claim: Federated learning is vulnerable to model poisoning attacks in which malicious clients corrupt the global model through manipulated model updates.

gap.claim: Existing defenses can resist only a small number of malicious clients, leaving defense against a large number of malicious clients as an open challenge.

contributions.claim: FLDetector detects malicious clients by checking the consistency of their model updates across multiple iterations.
The server predicts each client's update from historical updates and flags the client when received and predicted updates are inconsistent across multiple iterations.
FLDetector is intended to remove most malicious clients so that Byzantine-robust or provably robust federated learning methods can train with the remaining clients.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets covering multiple state-of-the-art model poisoning attacks and adaptive attacks tailored to FLDetector.
The authors report that FLDetector accurately detects malicious clients in those evaluated attacks.
The authors report that, after detected malicious clients are removed, existing Byzantine-robust federated learning methods can learn accurate global models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning is vulnerable to model poisoning attacks from malicious clients.
Existing robust federated learning defenses handle only a small number of malicious clients, leaving large-scale malicious participation unresolved.
FLDetector identifies malicious clients by detecting inconsistency between their received and historically predicted model updates across iterations.
Experiments on three benchmark datasets reportedly show accurate detection across multiple poisoning and adaptive attacks.
The authors report that robust federated learning methods can learn accurate global models after detected malicious clients are removed.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the three benchmark datasets.
The abstract does not provide detection metrics, model accuracy values, attack parameters, or client counts.
The abstract does not specify the prediction method, inconsistency threshold, or removal procedure.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, theoretical guarantees, or reproducibility details.
